A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WAVE study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Existing experiments and appendix material can be matched despite additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and question-answering results, training and architecture ablations, and a prompt-conditioned embedding case study.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds reverse-direction retrieval evaluations and an image-training experiment.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-Omni backbone, dual audio encoders, hierarchical feature fusion, and training objectives remain unchanged. Section 3.1 newly explains token interleaving, but does not establish a changed procedure. Image training is a supplementary experiment, not a revision of the main model.

E1.justification: Coverage expands to static images through MMEB-v1 image training and VisualNews text-to-image evaluation in Appendix F. Appendix C also adds video-to-text, audio-to-text, and audio-to-video evaluation, substantially broadening the tested retrieval directions beyond v1.

E2.justification: Matched experiments retain their comparator membership. The added reverse-direction evaluations reuse relevant existing comparators: GME 7B for video retrieval, Mei et al. (2024) for audio retrieval, and the authors' encoder-only model for audio-visual retrieval.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces a video-only versus mixed video/image training comparison, using nearly equal quantities of video and image data and the existing pure-visual setup. Previously stated main-experiment settings remain unchanged. The added resolution and inference descriptions disclose existing settings rather than establish protocol revisions.

E4.justification: New Appendix F tests whether adding image training benefits image retrieval while preserving video retrieval performance. Existing prompt, joint-training, feature-fusion, and dual-encoder analyses are retained; v1 Appendices B and C become v2 Appendices D and E.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added experiments continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 8 and 10 substantially extend the findings to reverse retrieval and image training. Reverse-direction Clotho retrieval scores WAVE at 24.5 versus 27.1 for Mei et al. (2024). The new training comparison reports VisualNews scores of 54.9 versus 74.8 and video-retrieval averages of 49.6 versus 50.2. Separately, Table 3 changes WAVE's overall score from 59.0 to 59.9 while retaining its component scores; Table 6 still reports 59.0. These are added comparisons and a reported-value revision, not demonstrated improvements between model versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives and derivations in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or other theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific contributions: unified audio-visual embeddings, prompt conditioning, hierarchical fusion, and strong retrieval and QA performance. Added appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly argues that strong video performance does not depend on exclusive video specialization and that image training is beneficial. Appendix C explains the practical motivation for previously emphasizing forward retrieval directions. Existing interpretations and limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies token interleaving, the 176400-pixel frame limit, inherited preprocessing settings, and retrieval/QA inference procedures. Its abstract reports released code and checkpoints and supplies a repository address, whereas v1 only promises release. Section 7 nevertheless retains the future-release statement.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Visual News citation, Liu et al. (2021), for the new image-retrieval evaluation. The related-work discussion and positioning against earlier embedding approaches otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained. v2 adds a token-interleaving explanation and appendices on inference, reverse retrieval, and image training, updates cross-references, and changes the publication header. Existing appendix studies are renumbered without substantive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds two result tables for reverse retrieval and image training. The original dual-encoder Table 8 becomes Table 9, and existing material shifts with pagination. Both figures and the structures of retained tables remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The reverse-direction evaluations and image-training experiment provide useful additional evidence for versatility, while implementation and inference details improve reproducibility. These gains are limited by the unexplained 59.9 versus 59.0 discrepancy between Tables 3 and 6 and inconsistent resource-release statements. The core method and principal conclusions remain stable.
